title: Daily kindness
tomorrow: deferred: not a yes, not a no. what do you do with the waiting?

cards: Six in the morning, four hours of sleep, and the first customer through the door wants to talk about the weather, his knee, and his granddaughter's recital. Amira's face does what tired faces do.
Then she remembers a hadith her dad has on a sticky note by the register, and smiles anyway. Is that fake? The tradition's answer runs through the body: the face, the voice, the hands.

teach.h: THE FACE: A SMILE IS CHARITY.
teach.b: Start with the face. In a report kept by al-Tirmidhi, the Prophet ﷺ says: your smile in the face of your brother is charity.
In Sahih Muslim he says: don't look down on any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face. A face is the first thing anyone receives from you, before a word is said.
Choosing what it gives, on four hours of sleep, isn't lying. It's the gift. Then the voice.

teach.h: THE VOICE: SPEAK KINDLY TO MANKIND.
teach.b: The Qur'an, telling the Children of Israel what was asked of them, includes in Pickthall's words: "speak kindly to mankind." Mankind. Not only family, not only people who share your faith.
And in Sahih al-Bukhari, the Prophet calls God ar-Rafiq, the Gentle, who loves gentleness in every matter. Gentleness is heard in a tone before it's understood in a sentence.
Then the hands: a door held, a cup handed over with both hands, a chair pulled out. So one kindness a day isn't a grand plan.
It's what the face, the voice and the hands do with the next person through the door.
On a good day, that's easy. On four hours of sleep, it's the charity.

how: Muslims often cite the hadith that a smile is charity; daily kindness is practiced in ordinary ways, greeting people warmly, helping a neighbor, speaking gently, and parents teach it to children as part of good character (akhlaq).

o: one kind thing a day, done with the face, voice and hands
kindness shown to family members and no one else
a yearly act of service at the mosque or a shelter

games.q: kindness, by the body — tap the pairs.
p: a good deed not to look down on

s: a hadith calls smiling at another person a charity
in al-Tirmidhi: your smile in the face of your brother is charity.
the Qur'an's call to speak kindly is only about fellow believers
the verse says speak kindly to mankind.
a smile only counts as kindness if you feel cheerful
the face is a gift you choose to give; on a hard day, choosing it is the charity.

games.q: 11pm. someone in your group project sends a curt, slightly rude message about your slide. you're tired and annoyed. what fits ar-Rafiq?
o: match their tone; being honest about it is a kindness too.
leave them on read until morning so they learn.
reply short and gentle, fix the slide, then go to sleep.
games.why: God is the Gentle and loves gentleness in every matter. gentleness doesn't mean agreeing; it shows up in the tone first.

practice: Unclench your jaw and let your shoulders drop. Let a small smile come to your face, even if it starts on purpose, and hold it softly for a few breaths.
Notice what changes in your breath or your chest, if anything, and keep the softness as you sit.

wordCard.voice: Daily kindness: one kind thing a day, carried by the face, the voice and the hands, and counted in the hadith as charity.

orig.note: Arabic: gentleness; ar-Rafiq, the Gentle, is a name of God in the hadith.

carryVoice: For the next person through the door: one kindness, face first. Eleven down, three to go.

sources.ref: Jami' al-Tirmidhi 1956 (your smile in the face of your brother is charity)
Sahih Muslim 2626 (do not belittle any good deed, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6927 (God is Rafiq and loves gentleness in all matters)
